Maintenance Report — MNT-0155-002

Asset: WELL-0155 (NE-08 Well 155, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 03 Mar 2023 08:00 · Finished: 03 Mar 2023 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 14 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0155-0020 on 2023-03-02 Report written: 05 Mar 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0155-0020 at 08:30 on 2023-03-02 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.6% of the pad area, estimated 1.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 190 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 152 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0155-002 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.53% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0155-022

Asset: WELL-0155 (NE-08 Well 155, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 05 Dec 2025 08:00 · Finished: 10 Dec 2025 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 117 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0155-0159 on 2025-12-04 Report written: 11 Dec 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0155-0159 showed the wellhead at 14.4 °C with the air at 10.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 190 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 152 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0155-022 (WS-06).
